extras.summary: Standard #3: 'built-in retention log gives us event replay at no extra implementation cost, which the team has flagged as a future need' is asserted as fact with no source for the team's stated need or the 'no extra cost' claim
Standard #6: reasoning doesn't fully support the exclusivity of the claim given #1 and #4
Standard #8: 'Kafka is the right choice' stated with more certainty than the evidence supports
Standard #8: confidence not aligned to evidence quality because cited evidence overshoots the actual requirement

rationale: Both reviews correctly position the BLUF, both misjudge review depth as Medium against the key's Full, and both land the same two headline findings (vendor-only sourcing and missing alternatives) with the identical 8,000/day-vs-1M/sec arithmetic; A additionally develops the 'enterprise tier' growth claim into a full weakness with a calibrated, ICD-203-style fix and separately catches the unsupported 'no extra cost'/unattributed team-need claim, whereas B only footnotes the growth claim in a hedged scorecard line (even rating it as tolerable for a spike) and rates the unsupported-claim standard as 'Good', missing it. A's fixes are concrete and proportionate across all three gold flaws, giving the author more complete and actionable coverage.
